description: Imagine the aroma of freshly baked bread filling your kitchen, a golden crust giving way to an airy, olive oil-infused crumb. This Focaccia Genovese, studded with fragrant rosemary and kissed with sea salt, transports you straight to the sun-drenched Ligurian coast. It's a simple yet profoundly satisfying Italian classic, perfect for sharing.

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the warm water and active dry yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy. This indicates the yeast is active and ready to work its magic.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: Add the flour and 10g of fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms. Gradually add 3 tablespoons (45ml) of the olive oil, incorporating it until the dough comes together. It will be sticky.

instructions.title: Knead and First Rise
instructions.text: Transfer the dough to a lightly floured surface and knead for about 8-10 minutes, until it becomes smooth and elastic. Alternatively, use a stand mixer with a dough hook for 5-7 minutes. Place the dough in a well-oiled bowl, turning to coat. Cover with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until doubled in size.

instructions.title: Shape and Dimple
instructions.text: Generously oil a 9x13 inch baking pan with 2 tablespoons (30ml) of olive oil. Gently transfer the risen dough to the pan, stretching it to fill the pan. If the dough resists, let it rest for 10 minutes before continuing. Use your fingertips to create deep dimples all over the surface of the dough, pushing down to the bottom of the pan.

instructions.title: Second Rise and Toppings
instructions.text: Drizzle the remaining 1 tablespoon (15ml) of olive oil over the dimpled focaccia. Sprinkle evenly with the chopped fresh rosemary and flaky sea salt. Cover loosely and let it rise again for 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy.

instructions.title: Bake to Golden Perfection
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 425F (220C). Bake the focaccia for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown on top and cooked through. The crust should be crisp and the interior soft and airy.

instructions.title: Cool and Serve
instructions.text: Once baked, remove the focaccia from the oven and transfer it to a wire rack to cool slightly. For an extra touch of flavor, you can drizzle a little more extra virgin olive oil over the warm focaccia before serving. Slice and enjoy warm or at room temperature.

tips: For the signature airy texture, do not over-knead the dough; a slightly sticky dough is desirable. Gentle handling preserves the air bubbles.
Use a high-quality extra virgin olive oil, as its flavor is central to authentic Focaccia Genovese. It's worth investing in a good one for this recipe.
If you don't have fresh rosemary, dried rosemary can be used, but reduce the quantity slightly as its flavor is more concentrated. Rehydrate it in a little olive oil first.
article:
Unlocking the secrets of authentic Italian baking can transform your kitchen into a haven of aromatic delights. Among the myriad of treasures Italy offers, few are as universally beloved and deceptively simple as Focaccia Genovese. This isn't just any flatbread; it's a culinary hug, a testament to the power of quality ingredients and traditional techniques. When infused with the fragrant essence of fresh rosemary and drenched in golden olive oil, it becomes a masterpiece: the Rosemary Focaccia Genovese. Imagine a soft, airy interior giving way to a crisp, salty crust, each bite bursting with savory notes. This article will guide you through creating this iconic Ligurian bread, from understanding its heritage to mastering the perfect dimple.

## What is Rosemary Focaccia Genovese?
At its heart, Focaccia Genovese is the quintessential flatbread from Genoa, the capital of Italy's Liguria region. Unlike its Roman cousin, pizza, focaccia is typically thicker, often baked in a rectangular pan, and characterized by its signature dimpled surface, which acts as tiny wells for pooling olive oil and capturing toppings. The "Genovese" distinction refers to its specific style: typically a higher hydration dough, resulting in a particularly soft and airy crumb, and a generous application of olive oil both in the dough and on top. The addition of fresh rosemary elevates this already delightful bread, infusing it with an earthy, piney aroma that perfectly complements the rich, fruity notes of extra virgin olive oil and the sharp bite of sea salt. It's more than just bread; it's a staple, often enjoyed plain as a snack, dipped in coffee for breakfast, or served alongside meals. Making your own Rosemary Focaccia Genovese allows you to experience a truly authentic piece of Italian culinary heritage right in your home.

## Ingredients for Authentic Focaccia Genovese
The beauty of Focaccia Genovese lies in its simplicity, making the quality of your ingredients paramount. To achieve that truly authentic flavor and texture, choose wisely.

*   **Flour:** For the best results, opt for Italian "00" flour, known for its fine texture and lower protein content, which contributes to a tender crumb. If "00" flour isn't available, a good quality unbleached all-purpose flour or strong bread flour will work well, though bread flour might yield a slightly chewier focaccia.
*   **Yeast:** Active dry or instant yeast. Active dry yeast will need to be proofed in warm water first, while instant yeast can be mixed directly with the dry ingredients.
*   **Water:** Lukewarm water (around 105-115°F / 40-46°C) is crucial for activating the yeast without killing it.
*   **Extra Virgin Olive Oil:** This is non-negotiable. Invest in a high-quality, fruity extra virgin olive oil. It's not just an ingredient; it's a defining flavor of Rosemary Focaccia Genovese, used generously in the dough, for oiling the pan, and drizzled over the top before baking.
*   **Salt:** Fine sea salt for the dough, and flaky sea salt (like Maldon) for sprinkling on top before baking. The flaky salt provides a delightful textural crunch and bursts of savory flavor.
*   **Fresh Rosemary:** Avoid dried rosemary if possible. Fresh rosemary sprigs, finely chopped, provide the most vibrant and aromatic flavor.
*   **Sugar (optional):** A tiny pinch of sugar can help activate the yeast, though it's not strictly necessary if your yeast is fresh.

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Perfect Rosemary Focaccia
Crafting the perfect Rosemary Focaccia Genovese is a rewarding experience. Follow these steps for a truly memorable bake:

1.  **Activate the Yeast (if using active dry):** In a large bowl, combine the lukewarm water, yeast, and a pinch of sugar (if using). Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active. If using instant yeast, you can skip this step and add it directly to the flour.
2.  **Combine Dry Ingredients:** In a separate large bowl, whisk together the flour and fine sea salt.
3.  **Mix the Dough:** Pour the activated yeast mixture (or water and instant yeast) and 2-3 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil into the flour mixture. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy, sticky dough forms.
4.  **Knead the Dough:** Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Knead for 8-10 minutes (or 5-7 minutes in a stand mixer with a dough hook) until the dough is smooth, elastic, and no longer sticky. It should pass the "windowpane test" – you should be able to stretch a small piece thin enough to see light through it without tearing.
5.  **First Rise:** Lightly oil a clean bowl with olive oil. Place the dough in the bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover the bowl tightly with plastic wrap or a damp kitchen towel. Let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.
6.  **Prepare the Pan:** Liberally coat a 9x13 inch (or similar size) baking sheet with extra virgin olive oil. Don't be shy; this oil contributes to the crispy bottom crust.
7.  **Shape the Dough:** Gently transfer the risen dough to the prepared baking sheet. Using your fingertips, gently press and stretch the dough to fill the pan, being careful not to deflate it too much. If the dough resists, cover it with plastic wrap and let it rest for 10-15 minutes before continuing to stretch.
8.  **Second Rise:** Once the dough fills the pan, cover it again and let it rise for another 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy.
9.  **Dimple and Top:** Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C). Once the dough has completed its second rise, generously drizzle another 2-3 tablespoons of olive oil over the surface. Using your oiled fingertips, create deep dimples all over the dough, pressing almost to the bottom of the pan. Sprinkle generously with chopped fresh rosemary and flaky sea salt.
10. **Bake:** Bake for 20-30 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and the bottom is crisp.
11. **Cool:** Transfer the Rosemary Focaccia Genovese to a wire rack to cool slightly. It's best enjoyed warm.

## Pro Tips for the Best Focaccia Genovese
Achieving bakery-quality Rosemary Focaccia Genovese at home is entirely possible with a few expert insights:

*   **Don't Skimp on Olive Oil:** This is perhaps the most critical tip. Olive oil is integral to focaccia's flavor, texture, and signature crisp crust. Use a generous amount both in the dough, for oiling the pan, and as a final drizzle.
*   **Hydration is Key:** Focaccia dough is typically quite sticky and wet. Don't be tempted to add too much extra flour during kneading, as this will result in a dry, dense focaccia. Embrace the stickiness; it contributes to the airy crumb.
*   **Proper Kneading:** Developing the gluten structure through thorough kneading is essential for that characteristic chewy, yet tender, texture.
*   **Deep Dimples:** When dimpling the dough, don't be afraid to press firmly. These dimples prevent large air bubbles from forming and create pockets for the olive oil and salt to collect, intensifying the flavor in every bite.
*   **Hot Oven, Quick Bake:** A high oven temperature ensures a quick bake, which helps create a beautifully crisp crust while keeping the interior soft and moist.
*   **Listen to Your Dough:** Dough rise times are approximate. Factors like room temperature can affect how quickly your dough proofs. Watch for it to double in size rather than strictly adhering to a timer.
*   **Fresh Rosemary:** As mentioned, fresh rosemary makes a significant difference. Its potent aroma and flavor are unparalleled.

## Serving Suggestions for Your Italian Focaccia
The versatility of Rosemary Focaccia Genovese is one of its most appealing qualities. Here are some delicious ways to enjoy your freshly baked bread:

*   **Simply Plain:** Warm focaccia, straight from the oven, is a delight on its own. The simple flavors of olive oil, rosemary, and sea salt are often all you need.
*   **Dipping:** Serve it with a small bowl of high-quality extra virgin olive oil, perhaps a splash of balsamic vinegar, for dipping.
*   **Appetizer:** It's a fantastic addition to any charcuterie board, cheese platter, or antipasto spread. Its robust flavor pairs wonderfully with cured meats, olives, and various cheeses.
*   **Sandwiches:** Slice the focaccia horizontally to create incredibly flavorful and satisfying sandwiches. Fill it with prosciutto, fresh mozzarella, roasted vegetables, or a simple caprese salad.
*   **Soup and Salad Accompaniment:** Tear off chunks to sop up hearty soups or serve alongside a crisp green salad for a complete meal.
*   **Breakfast/Brunch:** In Genoa, it's common to dip focaccia in coffee for breakfast! Try it with scrambled eggs, avocado, or a smear of ricotta for a unique brunch experience.

## Variations and Substitutions for Focaccia Genovese
While the classic Rosemary Focaccia Genovese is perfect as is, you can certainly experiment with variations to suit your taste or what you have on hand.

*   **Other Herbs:** While rosemary is traditional, you can substitute or add other fresh herbs like thyme, oregano, sage, or a mix of "herbes de Provence."
*   **Toppings Galore:** Beyond rosemary and sea salt, consider adding other toppings before baking:
    *   **Olives:** Kalamata, green, or black olives, halved or whole.
    *   **Cherry Tomatoes:** Halved cherry tomatoes pressed into the dimples.
    *   **Caramelized Onions:** Sweet and savory.
    *   **Garlic:** Thinly sliced garlic cloves or roasted garlic paste.
    *   **Flaky Sea Salt:** Experiment with flavored sea salts, such as smoked paprika or chili flakes.
*   **Cheese:** For an extra layer of richness, sprinkle some grated Parmesan, Pecorino Romano, or even small chunks of fresh mozzarella over the focaccia during the last 10 minutes of baking.
*   **Flour Alternatives:** While "00" or bread flour is ideal, you can substitute a portion (up to 25-30%) with whole wheat flour for a nuttier flavor and added fiber, though it might result in a slightly denser crumb. For gluten-free options, a good quality gluten-free bread flour blend designed for yeast baking can be used, often requiring specific adjustments to hydration and rise times.
*   **Sweet Focaccia:** While less common for the Genovese style, focaccia can be made sweet. Omit the rosemary and salt, add a little more sugar to the dough, and top with fruits like grapes, figs, or even a dusting of sugar and cinnamon.

Baking Rosemary Focaccia Genovese is an accessible and incredibly rewarding journey into Italian culinary tradition. With quality ingredients and a little patience, you'll soon be enjoying this aromatic, irresistible bread that transports you straight to the sun-drenched Ligurian coast. Buon appetito!
